title: Vaccination awareness
content: Vaccines help the immune system prepare for specific infections. Which vaccines a person needs depends on factors such as age, pregnancy, health conditions, occupation and travel. Keep a vaccination record and ask a qualified health professional or official vaccination service about the recommended schedule.

title: Healthy eating
content: A balanced diet can include a variety of vegetables and fruits, whole grains or other high-fibre foods, and suitable protein sources. Limit excess salt, added sugars and highly processed foods. Individual needs vary, so people with medical conditions should seek professional advice.

title: Physical activity
content: Regular physical activity supports overall health. Choose movement that is safe and realistic for your age and ability, such as walking or other enjoyable activities. Start gradually if you are inactive and seek professional guidance if you have health concerns.

title: Hygiene and infection prevention
content: Hand hygiene, safe food and water practices, ventilation, and staying home when acutely unwell can reduce the spread of some infections. Seek professional care when symptoms are severe, worsening or persistent.

title: Pregnancy and antenatal care
content: Antenatal care helps monitor the health of the pregnant person and baby and provides opportunities for prevention, screening and health education. Seek care promptly for warning signs such as heavy bleeding, severe pain, fainting, or severe breathing difficulty.

title: Child health
content: Children benefit from routine vaccination, nutrition, growth and development monitoring, and timely professional assessment when they are unwell. Caregivers should seek urgent help for severe breathing difficulty, unconsciousness, seizures, severe dehydration or other emergency warning signs.

title: Mental wellbeing
content: Mental wellbeing can be supported by regular sleep, social connection, physical activity, healthy routines and stress-management practices. Persistent distress or symptoms that interfere with daily life deserve professional support. Immediate self-harm risk requires urgent help.

title: Health information literacy
content: Reliable health information should be understandable, evidence-informed and transparent about uncertainty. Compare important claims with trusted public-health sources and qualified professionals rather than relying on social-media forwards or unverified messages.

title: Care navigation
content: When you need care, consider the urgency, the type of service needed, distance, operating hours and whether remote consultation is appropriate. Government telemedicine services can help people in locations where in-person access is difficult.

title: Tobacco and quitting
content: Avoiding tobacco reduces exposure to harmful substances. If you use tobacco and want to quit, support from a qualified health professional, quit programme or trusted cessation resource can make the process more manageable.

title: Tuberculosis (TB) awareness
content: TB is a bacterial infection spread mainly through the air. Common symptoms include a persistent cough lasting 3 or more weeks, coughing blood, unexplained weight loss, fever and night sweats. TB is treatable when diagnosed early and the full course of medication is completed. Free diagnosis and treatment are available through government health facilities in India.

title: Dengue fever awareness
content: Dengue is a viral illness spread by Aedes mosquitoes, often in urban and semi-urban areas. Symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, joint and muscle pain, rash, and mild bleeding. There is no specific antiviral treatment; management focuses on rest, hydration and professional monitoring. Seek care promptly for warning signs: severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, or rapid breathing.

title: Malaria awareness
content: Malaria is caused by a parasite transmitted through the bites of infected mosquitoes. Symptoms include fever, chills, headache, muscle aches and fatigue; severe malaria can affect the brain, kidneys and blood. Early diagnosis and prompt treatment are essential. Government health facilities in India provide diagnosis and treatment. Prevent mosquito bites with nets, repellent and protective clothing.

title: Diabetes prevention and awareness
content: Type 2 diabetes risk can be reduced through maintaining a healthy weight, regular physical activity, a diet low in added sugars and refined carbohydrates, and avoiding tobacco. People with risk factors such as family history, overweight, or age over 40 should consider periodic blood-sugar checks. Managing diagnosed diabetes requires professional guidance; do not change medication without consulting a qualified professional.

title: Heart health and cardiovascular prevention
content: Cardiovascular disease risk can be lowered by reducing salt and saturated fat intake, staying physically active, quitting tobacco, limiting alcohol, managing blood pressure and maintaining a healthy weight. Know the emergency warning signs: chest pain, pain spreading to arm or jaw, sudden breathlessness, sweating and dizziness — call 112 immediately for suspected heart attack.

title: Respiratory health and clean air
content: Indoor air pollution from cooking fires, tobacco smoke and poor ventilation can harm lung health over time. Using clean fuels, improving ventilation, and avoiding tobacco protect the lungs. Symptoms like a cough lasting more than 3 weeks, shortness of breath on mild exertion, or wheezing deserve professional evaluation. Severe breathing difficulty is always an emergency — call 112.

title: Fever — general guidance
content: Fever is a common sign that the body is responding to infection. Rest, adequate fluids and appropriate clothing help with comfort. Seek professional care for a fever above 39°C (102°F) in adults, any fever in infants under 3 months, fever lasting more than 3 days, or fever with stiff neck, rash, severe headache, confusion or breathing difficulty. Do not use aspirin for fever in children.

title: Diarrhoea and oral rehydration
content: Diarrhoea can cause dangerous dehydration, especially in children and older adults. Oral rehydration solution (ORS) — available in pharmacies and government health facilities — helps replace lost fluids and salts. Seek urgent care if diarrhoea lasts more than 2 days, contains blood, or if there are signs of severe dehydration: very dry mouth, no urination, rapid breathing, confusion or unconsciousness.

title: Medicine safety — general principles
content: Before taking any medicine, check the label or prescription for dosage instructions, expiry date, and storage requirements. Inform your healthcare provider about allergies and other medicines you take to avoid harmful interactions. Never share prescription medicines. Ask a pharmacist or qualified professional if you are unsure. For overdose or severe allergic reaction (difficulty breathing, swelling, hives), seek emergency help immediately.

title: Mental health support — when to seek help
content: Emotional difficulties such as prolonged sadness, hopelessness, inability to carry out daily activities, persistent anxiety, or thoughts of self-harm are signs that professional support is needed. Talking to a trusted person or a qualified mental health professional is a positive step. In a crisis, contact a mental health helpline or go to the nearest emergency service. Remember: seeking help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
